newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican Fegusa to export 90,000 T fertilizer in 97.
newsitem.headline: Mexican Fegusa to export 90,000 T fertilizer in 97.

text.p: Mexico's leading fertilizer producer Fertilizers Guadalajara (Fegusa) will export in 1997 about 90,000 tonnes of ammonium sulfates to New Zealand, El Salvador and Thailand, a company director said.
Fegusa holds about 35 percent market share in nitrogen and phosfate based fertilizer production in Mexico. In 1996 the company exported almost 36,000 tonnes of ammonium sulfate.

"Of the 90,000 tonnes of ammonium sulfate that we aim to export, we already have destined 40,000 (tonnes) for El Salvador and New Zealand," Fegusa Director General Jose Gomez Laurean told Reuters in an interview.
He added the remainder will be sent to Thailand and that the company is also in negotiations with importers from Peru, Nicaragua, Guatemala, the Dominican Republic, Costa Rica and Brazil.
Mexico produces about five million tonnes of nitrogen and phosfate based fertilizers per year, while domestic consumption is about 3.5 million tonnes per year, Gomez said.
"This year we plan to see production above 360,000 tonnes of ammonium sulfates and of simple supersulfates we have projected 90,000 tonnes this year," he added.
Gomez said Fegusa also plans to raise its output of a new birdseed to substitute for U.S. imports of the feed.
